article.title: A book begins before its first sentence.
article.intro: An editorial choice in Todos ou nenhum? — Book I: beginning with a sheet of paper.
paragraphs: A sheet bends under its own weight. Joined to others, it becomes part of a structure: pages, stitching, glue, a spine. The prologue follows this transformation before the first poem.
The opening brings together the book we read and the object we hold. It directs attention to the gap that must open between two pages before a sentence becomes visible.

This relationship runs through the volume. Iron, glass, light and paper remain specific materials with their own behaviours and limits. Bringing them close to human experience also requires acknowledging where the comparison ends.
Engravings interrupt the verbal sequence. Colour pages change the field of attention before a longer prose piece. Form shapes the pace without needing to explain the text.
The prologue offers a way in. Holding an opening precedes reading; the relationships that follow belong to each reader.

repertoire.heading: Saving is not the same as building a repertoire.
paragraphs: A saved image still awaits a question. The work begins when we return to it: what caught our attention, in what context was it made, and what changes beside another image?
Repertório Fóscolo is a series about that return. A detail in a book, a landscape or a framing choice can open a relationship. Naming the source and testing the connection are part of reading.

editorial: Books, images and questions keep changing when they meet a reader. Explore the reflections that accompany our editorial work.

An edition gives a work its form; circulation opens further possibilities. A passage gains meaning through an experience, and an image can lead to a question the text has not yet posed. The book continues in that conversation.
The feed passes. Some things should not.
Gathering a reflection on a page lets readers return to it, follow its connections and read beyond the pace of a feed. The Journal gives editorial choices and reading paths more time.
Emptiness is also an editorial decision

A page is made of more than printed words. Margins, distances and the position of the text guide the eye. Space around words shapes rhythm: it creates pauses, establishes hierarchies and changes the attention given to each passage.
Saving is not building a repertoire

Keeping a reference is a beginning. Building a repertoire means returning, comparing and asking why a form works. A margin, an image sequence or a relationship between text and landscape becomes useful when we can think with it.

When research takes book form, its questions enter other reading situations. In Notes on Care, Risk & Knowledge, history, fragments and images offer different ways into care, risk and knowledge. Readers can connect these questions to experiences the research could not anticipate.

“The rest was in neither of them.” This encounter accompanies Todos ou nenhum?: a life and a practice of writing also emerge from relationships between experiences, questions and choices. Poems and essayistic chronicles offer different rhythms for following these encounters.

circulationArticle.title: Publishing does not bring things to an end.
circulationArticle.intro: What changes when a book no longer belongs only to the table where it was made?
paragraphs: For a while, a book lives inside a small circuit: writing, selecting, cutting, revising, designing and printing. Almost everything can still be brought back to the table and changed.

Publication changes that scale. The book enters an envelope, passes through other hands, reaches a shelf the publisher does not know and meets experiences that were absent while it was being written. A secondary passage for the writer can become the centre of somebody else’s reading.

Circulation is therefore more than physical movement. A book circulates when it creates unforeseen relationships: an image meets a memory, an argument meets disagreement, a question reaches another field of experience.

For an independent publisher, this passage belongs to publication itself. Finishing a file or producing an object is not enough. Publishing also means creating the conditions for a work to leave the place where it began without controlling what happens next.
Publication, then, does not close the work. It closes only one stage of control. The rest begins when the book is read by someone who was not at the table.

placeArticle.title: From where does this table look at the world?
placeArticle.intro: Belo Horizonte is more than the address in the colophon.
paragraphs: Every publisher works from somewhere. Even when a book deals with questions that cross countries, institutions and historical periods, what first appears important begins in very concrete relationships.

Fóscolo & Company is edited in Belo Horizonte. Archives, universities, libraries, movement through the city, Pampulha and conversations taking place here form part of the repertoire through which books are read and prepared.
This does not mean turning the city into compulsory scenery or publishing only about Minas Gerais. It means giving up the fiction of a neutral point of view. Editorial choices have a geography too.

Circulation moves in the opposite direction: a book can leave a place without remaining trapped by it. It may reach another city, institution or language and meet questions that did not exist at the table where it began.
Saying where the work is made does not reduce a publisher’s reach. It makes visible the point from which it chooses to look.

spaceArticle.title: Empty space is also an editorial decision.
spaceArticle.intro: Margins, distance and pause also organise a reading.
paragraphs: A page is made of more than what it prints. Before reading a sentence, the eye encounters margins, distances, alignments, blocks and interruptions.
These intervals establish hierarchies. Bringing two elements close together can make them appear to belong to the same argument; separating them can create a pause or prevent an easy association.

White space is therefore not an absence of work. In a book combining research, poetry, photography or essayistic prose, it can be the difference between piling materials together and allowing each form to retain its own presence.
There is also a limit. Emptiness should not operate as prestige decoration or as a way of making little content appear more important. Form must answer to the rhythm and function of the page.

Editing also means deciding what will not occupy space. Sometimes the best intervention is to leave enough distance for a reader to perceive a relationship without being forced to understand it in only one way.

repertoireArticle.title: The uncertainty is in the first sentence.
repertoireArticle.intro: A reading of the opening of Machado de Assis’s “Missa do Galo”.
repertoireArticle.quote: Nunca pude entender a conversação que tive com uma senhora, há muitos anos, contava eu dezessete, ela trinta.
paragraphs: The first sentence does not promise to clarify a conversation. It begins with the impossibility of understanding it completely.
The narrator looks back on an old episode knowing more than he knew at seventeen, yet distance does not become certainty. Memory supplies details without automatically resolving their meaning.
The opening is a useful reminder that ambiguity is not the same thing as missing information. A text can offer many elements while preserving more than one possible relationship between them.
Reading the sentence again changes the weight of simple words: “never”, “understand”, “many years ago”. The time of memory enters the story before we even know what was said that night.

This is the kind of return Repertório Fóscolo tries to practise: choose a concrete detail, return to it, contextualise what can be said and keep visible the point at which interpretation remains open.
